subject: AcreetionOS Update — June 26, 2026
body:
Our continuous integration pipeline has just been fine-tuned again, with recent changes making our release process even more reliable and efficient, and you can find all the details on our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html. This improvement is a great example of how our community-driven development process is always improving, and we're excited to see the impact it will have on our users.

Development
The development team has been focused on fine-tuning our continuous integration pipeline, with recent commits like the use of per-pipeline staging directories to avoid publish races between concurrent builds, and the use of relative symlinks for latest.iso so it resolves on the host web root. These changes are crucial in ensuring that our users receive the latest updates in a timely and reliable manner. For more information on our development process, you can visit our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html.

Community
Our community has been actively exploring the new features and improvements brought by the recent Emacs 31.1 release, and we're seeing a lot of interest in the removal of the old GUI. If you're looking for more information on how to get the most out of Emacs on AcreetionOS, you can check out our documentation page at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html. Additionally, our community is always discussing the latest security updates, such as the recent stable kernel set, and you can stay up-to-date with the latest news on our website at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html.
